results.result: Acute depletion of TBP in mouse embryonic stem cells has no global effect on ongoing Pol II transcription. Treatment with IAA for 6 hours resulted in >90% TBP depletion and >80% decrease in TBP occupancy at promoters, yet Pol II occupancy and nascent RNA levels (measured by NET-seq) remained largely unchanged across the genome, with only 29 genes showing significant downregulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C36-C52, and C147 collectively demonstrate that TBP depletion does not globally affect Pol II transcription. Multiple orthogonal methods (western blot, immunofluorescence, ChIP-qPCR, CUT&Tag, NET-seq) confirm efficient TBP depletion (C36-C41), while Pol II CUT&Tag and NET-seq data show no global changes in transcription (C42-C49). DGE analysis confirms that 99.9% of genes are unaffected (C49), with only a small subset showing changes (C50-C52). The convergence of evidence from multiple techniques strongly supports this major finding.

results.result: Acute TBP depletion severely impairs RNA Polymerase III transcription at tRNA genes. Upon TBP depletion, Pol III occupancy and nascent RNA levels at tRNA genes decreased substantially, while Pol III protein levels remained unchanged, demonstrating that TBP is required for Pol III transcription in mESCs.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C54-C61, and C148 provide strong evidence that TBP is required for Pol III transcription. Western blot confirms Pol III protein levels are unaffected (C54-C55), while CUT&Tag and NET-seq data show major decreases in Pol III occupancy and activity at tRNA genes (C56-C59). This contrasts with the lack of effect on Pol II (C61), providing an internal control that validates the TBP depletion system. The consistency across multiple tRNA genes and replicates supports this conclusion.

results.result: Pol II transcriptional induction occurs normally upon TBP depletion. Both heat shock-induced genes and retinoic acid-induced genes show normal induction patterns when TBP is depleted, as measured by Pol II CUT&Tag and NET-seq, with no significant differences in gene expression between TBP-depleted and control conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C62-C80, and C149 demonstrate that TBP is not required for gene induction. Heat shock experiments (C63-C70) and retinoic acid differentiation experiments (C73-C79) both show normal gene induction upon TBP depletion, as confirmed by CUT&Tag, NET-seq, and DGE analysis. GO analysis confirms proper heat shock response (C66). The use of two independent gene induction systems strengthens the conclusion that TBP is dispensable for both ongoing transcription and gene activation (C80).

results.result: TBP-independent transcription is not due to functional redundancy with the TBP paralog TRF2. Although TRF2 binds to all active promoters in mESCs and its binding correlates with TBP and Pol II levels, knockout of TRF2 combined with TBP depletion has no global effect on Pol II transcription, demonstrating that TRF2 does not functionally replace TBP.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C5, C81-C99, C150 provide strong evidence that TRF2 is not functionally redundant with TBP. HA-TRF2 CUT&Tag shows TRF2 binds to all active promoters (C86-C89), but TRF2 knockout combined with TBP depletion shows no global effect on Pol II transcription (C94-C95) or cell viability (C96-C97). DGE analysis confirms minimal effects (C92-C93), and qRT-PCR shows no change in nascent transcription (C90-C91). The combination of genetic knockout and acute depletion provides robust evidence against functional redundancy.

results.result: The TFIID complex can form when TBP is depleted. TAF4 IP-MS analysis shows that all TAF subunits of the TFIID complex are present at similar levels in control and TBP-depleted conditions, with no significant differences in enrichment. Gel filtration analysis confirms that TFIID does not dissociate into smaller subcomplexes upon TBP depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C100-C112, C151, C178 demonstrate that TFIID can form without TBP. TAF4 IP-MS identifies all TAF subunits at similar levels in control and IAA-treated cells (C103-C105), with statistical analysis showing no significant differences (C105). Gel filtration confirms the complex remains intact (C107-C108), and relative stoichiometries are unchanged (C109-C110). The convergence of IP-MS and gel filtration data provides strong support for TFIID formation in the absence of TBP.

results.result: TAF4 binding is reduced when TBP is depleted. TAF4 CUT&Tag shows approximately 65% decrease in TAF4 occupancy at promoters upon TBP depletion, with genes experiencing the largest TBP depletion also showing the greatest TAF4 reduction. However, this decrease in TAF4 does not correlate with decreased Pol II occupancy.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C122-C130, C154 demonstrate reduced TAF4 binding upon TBP depletion. CUT&Tag data shows moderate decreases at specific loci (C122-C123) and genome-wide (C124-C125), quantified as ~65% reduction (C125). Pearson correlation and k-means clustering confirm the effect (C126-C128). Importantly, scatter plot analysis shows genes with decreased TAF4 do not show decreased Pol II (C129), supporting the robustness of the Pol II machinery. Multiple analytical approaches converge on this conclusion.

results.result: TFIIA binding is reduced when TBP is depleted. TAF4 IP-MS shows significantly decreased TFIIA-γ peptides upon TBP depletion, and TFIIA CUT&Tag shows approximately 60% decrease in TFIIA occupancy at promoters. This confirms that TBP mediates the TFIID-TFIIA interaction, yet Pol II transcription remains unaffected despite reduced TFIIA binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C131-C141, C145, C152, C154 demonstrate reduced TFIIA binding upon TBP depletion. TAF4 IP-MS shows significantly decreased TFIIA-γ co-precipitation (C132-C133), not due to altered protein levels (C134). TFIIA CUT&Tag shows global decrease in occupancy (C135-C137), quantified as ~60% reduction (C137). Pearson correlation and k-means clustering confirm the effect (C138-C139). Scatter plot analysis shows TFIIA decrease does not affect Pol II (C140), and TFIIA correlates with TAF4 changes (C141). Multiple orthogonal approaches support this conclusion.

results.result: The Pol II machinery is sufficiently robust to sustain TBP-independent transcription. Despite reduced TAF4 and TFIIA binding upon TBP depletion, Pol II occupancy and nascent RNA levels remain unaffected, suggesting inherent robustness in the Pol II transcriptional machinery that compensates for TBP depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C146, C155-C156, C196 represent the central conclusion drawn from the collective data. The observation that Pol II transcription continues normally (C1, C155) despite reduced TAF4 (C7) and TFIIA (C8) binding provides strong evidence for robustness in the Pol II machinery (C9, C146, C156). This conclusion is well-supported by the convergence of multiple lines of evidence showing maintained Pol II activity despite perturbations to the canonical PIC assembly pathway.

results.result: TAF1 binding is unaffected by TBP depletion. TAF1 CUT&Tag shows no major changes in TAF1 occupancy at promoters upon TBP depletion, with high correlation between control and IAA-treated samples. K-means clustering confirms that even genes with the largest TBP depletion show no change in TAF1 binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C153, C113-C121 demonstrate that TAF1 binding is unaffected by TBP depletion. CUT&Tag data shows similar TAF1 levels at specific loci (C116) and genome-wide (C117), with Pearson correlation confirming high similarity between conditions (C118). K-means clustering and scatter plot analysis show no correlation between TBP depletion and TAF1 changes (C119-C120). The differential effect on TAF1 versus TAF4 (C153) provides important mechanistic insight into TFIID dynamics.

results.result: The mAID system achieves substantial but incomplete TBP depletion, leaving approximately 10,000-20,000 TBP molecules in cells with ~27,185 active genes. This level of depletion is insufficient to provide one TBP molecule per active TSS, yet Pol II transcription continues normally while Pol III transcription is severely impaired, validating the specificity of the depletion system.
results.evaluation: Claims C159-C164 provide important context for interpreting the results. The calculation that remaining TBP molecules are insufficient for one per active TSS (C163) strengthens the conclusion of TBP-independent transcription. The differential effect on Pol III (C164) serves as an internal control validating the depletion system. However, the incomplete depletion (C159) is a limitation that should be acknowledged when interpreting the functional role of TBP at promoters (C165).

results.result: Background on transcription initiation and the established role of TBP. The manuscript reviews established knowledge about PIC assembly, TBP's role in transcription, and previous findings in yeast and mammalian systems that established TBP as essential for transcription.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C25 represent established scientific knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These claims provide necessary background context for understanding the significance of the current findings. The citations to prior work appear appropriate and accurately represent the established understanding of TBP's role in transcription that the current study challenges.

results.result: Potential mechanisms for TBP-independent transcription. The manuscript outlines three hypothetical mechanisms: (1) TBP required only for initial activation, (2) TBP paralogs functionally replacing TBP, and (3) TAF-containing complexes facilitating transcription without TBP, supported by prior literature on each mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C35 represent hypotheses and established knowledge about potential mechanisms. The hypotheses (C26, C28, C32) are clearly stated as possibilities to be tested. The supporting literature (C27, C29-C31, C33-C35) is appropriately cited. These claims provide the rationale for the experimental approaches taken in the study.

The manuscript reviews established knowledge about Pol III targets, TRF2 properties across species, TFIID assembly, and evidence for robustness in transcriptional machinery from prior studies.

results.result: Discussion of limitations and speculative mechanisms. The manuscript acknowledges that the results do not provide information on TBP's functional role when recruited to promoters, and proposes several speculative mechanisms for TBP-independent transcription, including evolutionary redundancy, unique chromatin landscape of ESCs, TFIID dynamics, and PIC dynamics.
results.evaluation: Claims C165-C168, C173, C175, C177, C182, C184-C185, C187, C197-C198, C200 represent limitations, speculation, and discussion points. C165 appropriately acknowledges a limitation. The speculative mechanisms (C166-C167, C173, C175, C182, C184-C185, C187, C197-C198, C200) are clearly presented as possibilities rather than conclusions. C168 and C177 represent the authors' final conclusions qualified by the level of depletion achieved. These claims are appropriately tentative given the data.

results.result: Correlation analysis of TBP, Pol II, TAF4, TAF1, TFIIA, and NET-seq data. Heatmaps and average plots arranged by decreasing TBP occupancy show that TBP correlates strongly with transcription levels and other GTFs in control conditions, and that highly TBP-bound genes show the greatest reduction in TFIIA and TAF4 but no change in Pol II and TAF1 upon TBP depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C142-C144 describe integrative analysis combining multiple datasets. The correlation between TBP and transcription/GTFs in control conditions (C142) validates the experimental system. The differential effects on TFIIA/TAF4 versus Pol II/TAF1 in highly TBP-bound genes (C143-C144) provide important mechanistic insight. This analysis is supported by the heatmap data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3D and strengthens the overall conclusions.

results.result: TRF2 binding properties in mESCs. CUT&Tag results show that TRF2 binds to all active promoters in mESCs with binding levels correlating strongly to both TBP and Pol II, and that depletion of TBP in TRF2 knockout cells has no global effect on Pol II transcription.
results.evaluation: Claims C172 and C176 describe key observations about TRF2. C172 is supported by HA-TRF2 CUT&Tag data showing genome-wide binding and correlation analysis. C176 is supported by Pol II CUT&Tag in TRF2 knockout cells with TBP depletion. These observations are important for ruling out TRF2 functional redundancy and are well-supported by the data presented.
